scenes.say: Add one to a long row of nines, and every column flips. Why do language models lose that carry? And how does a tiny model never lose it?

scenes.headline: How a small model adds at any length, provably
scenes.sub: A 0.8B model, a sheet, and a three-cell window
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Zephyrine! This is Sketchpad: exact long arithmetic from a tiny model, with a certificate.

scenes.title: Why the carry gets lost
scenes.say: Chapter one. Why the carry gets lost.

scenes.title: Why long sums go wrong
scenes.say: A model trained on short sums usually struggles on long ones. The literature points at three suspects.

items.say: Position. A model trained on twenty-digit sums has never seen column three hundred.
The carry. One carry can depend on every digit to its right, and a forward pass has fixed depth.
Chain of thought writes steps down. But step nine hundred reads nine hundred steps of history nobody tested.

scenes.title: A sheet and a window
scenes.sub: Keep the scratchpad, take the history away
scenes.say: Chapter two. A sheet and a window.

steps.say: The system has three parts. The sheet holds everything: operands, carries, the answer. The runtime crops one column, three cells tall.
Qwen three point five, zero point eight billion, with a small adapter, reads that strip as an image. Nothing else is in its prompt.
steps.term: Pinned sheet: the prompt is the view, nothing else

steps.say: It answers a digit, a carry, and the next operation.
Plain code paints the answer and moves the window. The model is the transition function of a Turing machine.
The project's own animation. The window reads three cells of one column.
The model answers a digit, a carry and the next step. The runtime stamps it, and the window moves on.

legend: The hard case: a carry chain through every column
One column: view, one token, paint, move left
The chain is written on the sheet, never computed in one pass

steps.say: Here's the hard case, the one that breaks a fixed-depth forward pass: nine nines, plus one.

steps.term: View: the three cells the model is shown
steps.say: The window shows the first column: no carry, a nine over a one. The model answers one token. a means digit zero, carry one. The runtime writes the zero, puts the carry one column left, and moves.
Now the view is a carry over a nine. Same kind of step, again and again, all the way along. The carry chain is never computed inside one pass. It is written on the sheet.
The last column is just the carry. Then all three cells are blank, and the model says halt.

scenes.title: Checking every view
scenes.sub: A finite list stands in for every length

scenes.text: Each step sees only three cells. Check every view, and every length is checked.
scenes.say: Here's the idea. Every step reads only a three-cell view. So checking every possible view checks every run, of every length.

scenes.title: Counting what the model can see

steps.term: View: the three cells the model is shown
steps.say: In addition, the carry is blank or one, and each digit cell is blank or a digit. Two hundred and forty-two views, at any length.
Multiplication's five tables add one thousand five hundred and fifty-three.
Subtraction, estimation for division, and a decrement add six hundred and fifty-one.
Two thousand four hundred and forty-six views, in all.

scenes.title: One step, forever
scenes.say: Every step has the same shape.

parts.note: the runtime shows a view from a finite list
parts.say: The runtime shows a view, from a finite list.

parts.note: the model: a function of the view alone
parts.say: The answer depends on that view alone.

parts.note: same answer, same next sheet: induct on steps
parts.say: So matching the table on every view means matching every run, step by step.

steps.term: Margin: right logit minus the best wrong one
steps.say: Checked means a margin. Every view is scored on the device, and each must put the right token ahead.
All two thousand four hundred and forty-six pass. The weakest, five plus six, leads by three point zero two logits.

scenes.title: One broken view, random sums
scenes.note: exact answers with view 5 over 6 corrupted
scenes.say: Why not just test sums? The article broke that one view. Ten-digit sums still came out right ninety-four percent of the time. Enumerating the views catches it with certainty.

scenes.title: What the proof covers
scenes.say: Chapter four. What the proof covers.

left.title: Chain of thought
items: Each step reads all earlier steps
left.say: Chain of thought grows its context. No finite test certifies it.

right.title: Pinned sheet
items: A finite check covers every length
right.say: The pinned sheet has a fixed list of inputs. Check them all.

steps.say: The paper proves it in Lean: the model's run equals the reference run, for every length, if and only if it agrees on every view.
And when a step can read its own history, a decoder can pass every test up to some length, then fail just past it.

scenes.title: Where the guarantee lives
scenes.say: So what did Lean prove? A chain of three links, and only the middle one is formal.

items.say: The model is right on every view: a measurement, on one GPU path.
Right on every view implies right at every length: the Lean theorem.
And the runtime only ever shows table views: assumed, and asserted at every step.

scenes.text: Bound what each step can see, and exactness at every length becomes a finite list you can check.
scenes.mark: a finite list you can check
scenes.say: Bound what each step can see, and exactness at every length becomes a finite list you can check.
